sections.label: Fixes
sections.description: Bugs: a bomber with no muzzles stopped other units' targeting; aircraft inside a shield's bubble hit everything under it; the Chosen T2 point defence couldn't raise its barrel above level; T1 bombs expired before they could land.

sections.label: Economy
sections.description: Commanders make 3 alloys and 30 energy a second (were 5 and 50) and start you with full storage, 500 alloys and 5000 energy (was half, 250 and 2500). T2 and T3 extractors make 5 and 15 (were 4 and 10); T1 and T2 generators make 20 and 600 energy (were 10 and 300), and T3 ones cost 2800 alloys (were 5000). Alloy Furnaces use 2000 energy a second (were 1000). The Guardian Crucible costs 3x as much and takes 3x as long to build (150000 alloys), and its death explosion does 50000 damage out to 40. Factories cost 200 alloys (were 150), upgrading one to T2 costs 1000 (was 500) over 90 s (was 80) and to T3 4000 (was 2000), and T3 tanks and the Guardian T3 raider cost 30% less. T2 radar uses 250 energy a second (was 150) and T3 radar costs 2800 alloys (was 700) and 1400 energy a second (was 350); EDA and Chosen T3 radar see 750 and 850 (were 450 and 550). Wrecks reclaim 3x as fast and last 6 minutes (were 3). Land units cost 6 energy per alloy (were 10) and T1-T3 aircraft 40 (were 20, Chosen 10), and engineers have less than half their health.

sections.label: Commanders
sections.description: The EDA and Guardian commanders' missiles fly at once and steer at where the target is going, in smaller, faster volleys: they hit moving units as often as the Chosen commander does.

sections.label: Artillery
sections.description: Artillery leads moving targets (it couldn't hit anything moving in a straight line); the three factions' T1 artillery are brought level.

sections.label: Defences
sections.description: Point defences see as far as they shoot, and T1 point defences are tougher: they beat their cost in T1 tanks, while T1 artillery still outranges them. T2 point defences are much tougher and hit harder, and the Chosen T3 one hits much harder. Shields cost more and hold less: T2 300 alloys for 6000 (were 150 for 10000), T3 1000 for 15000 (were 600 for 20000), and use twice the energy to run.

sections.label: Unit tuning
sections.description: The Chosen Jager toned down and the other T2 raiders brought up, so T2 beats its cost in T1 without crushing it; the three T1 tanks brought level; T3 tanks move as fast as T1 tanks with quicker guns, and the Guardian T3 raider is faster still and lighter; T4 bots move at 2.25-3 (were 2; none faster than T3 tanks; the Chosen big bot keeps the game's 1) and are game enders: 10000-25000 alloys with health and damage to match, less for the ones whose splash and range already win fights; the EDA railgun sniper reaches 80.

changes.name: Inertia
changes.label: projectile lifetime (s)
why: T1 bombs lived 2 seconds at speed 20, about 40 range, while the bombers release from up to 60. They now live long enough to land. Not the Chosen Comet, which the game reworked in 0.0.1.21.1 to drop its bomb from 10. (T3 bombs had the same fix until 0.2.9; the game's new flight patterns may have fixed them, to be tested.)

changes.name: Redoubt
changes.label: max barrel elevation (deg)
why: The Chosen T2 point defence (Redoubt) shot the ground: its model's barrel bone rests about 55 degrees nose-down, and it may only pitch up 45, so it could never raise the barrel to level. It never came on target (0% in tests at 20-47 range, other T2 point defences 48-94%). It may pitch up 100 now and rests level. (Game 0.0.1.21.1 turns the model's real yaw bone, which this patch used to fix, and lets it pitch up 55: just enough to reach level, never above it.)

Its range (24) stays well short of a T3 tank's (34).

changes.name: Behemoth
changes.label: cost
why: T4s are game enders for long 512 games that become spammable as the game goes on: they cost 10000-25000 alloys (2-3x what they did, energy 6 per alloy), and their health and damage are raised so that per alloy they beat the average T3 tank (15.8 health and 0.49 damage a second per alloy, after this patch's T3 discount) by 10%, or match it for the 60-100 range ones (Djinn, Chosen big bot) - then cut to 0.8x of that in 0.2.6, because one T4 keeps all its damage until it dies while a T3 army loses damage with every tank, so equal stats per alloy played as far stronger. The Quasar is matched against T3 artillery and keeps its health. Damage counts every muzzle and salvo (my arithmetic on the templates); death explosions are unchanged. EDA Behemoth: 10000 alloys (was 3696), 136000 health (was 72000) and weapon damage as listed. In 0.2.7 health went to 0.8x again and damage against the ground was cut by how much each T4 gets from splash (radius 3-4 hits several bunched T3 tanks) and from out-ranging T3 tanks (34): the Chosen big bot to 0.5x, the Ares, Centaur and Tripod to 0.6x, the Djinn to 0.75x, the rest to 0.9x, then both raised together (the same factor on health and ground damage, 1.13-1.34x) to about 0.8x a T3 tank's health x damage per alloy, splash and range counted, so one T4 (keeping all its damage until it dies) beats its cost in T3 tanks clearly but not by a mile. Splash counts: the big bot's radius-3 shells hit several tanks, the beam bot hits one, so the beam bot gets more health and damage per alloy. Anti-air weapons on T4s are unchanged.
